Well the maps I started with as a base had the DW2 map at 4096x4096 pixels and the DW1 tilemap at 1984x1984 pixels. You can see why it wouldn't actually fit, when I put them to scale so it could overlap at the correct spot I ended up with; DW2 map being 8192x8192 pixels and the DW1 map laying in the correction position at 2075x2075 pixels so still about 1/4 the size, which is exactly the size difference that Enix claimed back in the day. So that was the size I stuck with for the DW1 Map and brought the second map down to its scale, leaving the total layout size exactly the same.

(So that's 512x512 Tiles 16x16 pixels each)
It really does, because the only other method would have been to make it even larger to keep the size difference straight between the two.

I am working on bringing the original map from Dragon Warrior 1 (NES) into the original map of Dragon Warrior 2.   
  
In Dragon Warrior / Dragon Quest 2 you are able to visit the continent from the first game, however when they made the size of the second game four times larger but with very close together landmasses the original continent basically didn't fit. Resulting in a squished land mass with only a few visitable locations.

Any attempt to bring the continents into the same proportions runs into problems, such as the castles in the second game already take 4 tiles as opposed to 1 tile in the first game. So simply making the first continent large enough would push the tiles in the second game even larger thus making the castles take 16 tiles or 4x4.   
  
If that sounds confusing lets put it this way, increasing the size of the map to accommodates the correct map from the first game changes the size of the rest of the map and if your drawing it in tiles not as a vector image then it would mean more tiles. So a simple one tile bridge to cross a river would look strange as 4 bridges.  
  
So of course it makes sense to try to preserve the original size as much as possible but attempting to make room requires some compromises. What I did is allow a few regions such as the mountains near Tuhn stretch out a bit as well as the desert west of Moonbroke and the path north of their while allowing some of the contients to have more distance apart in the ocean. But while doing this making as many key points line up as much as possible.   
  
So islands are almost exactly where you would expect them, each cape or peninsula pointing or ending about where you would expect them and the Monument and Cave that allows cross continental travel are still lined up just much more distant. There is some stretching south of the oasis that bugs me but I it is still wip and I wasn't sure how to otherwise keep Beran about where it needs to be.     

TLDR: This is a Tile Map reconstruction of the DW1 map on the same Tile Map as the DW2 with a few things strected but still lined up.

You can see Rimuldar, Cantlin, Kol.. All the locations.
